title: erophila verna subsp. macrosperma
intro: Erophila verna subsp. macrosperma, commonly known as Spring Whitlow-grass, is a plant species within the Brassicaceae family. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its health benefits, which include its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antispasmodic properties. The therapeutic actions of Spring Whitlow-grass include reducing inflammation and pain, as well as its ability to treat respiratory issues such as coughs and bronchitis. The bioactive constituents of Spring Whitlow-grass include glucosinolates, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been reported to have antioxidant, anti-cancer, and neuroprotective effects.
